audit.whatIsWrong: The diff token says HARD while diffRating says 4/10, the tone is the green favoured colour, and breakdown.difficulty and report[14] both say 'Favoured matchup'. The level chart also disagrees with the mirrored Dr. Mundo audit at four rows.
audit.why: One field said hard and four said favoured, with a 60% win rate behind them — the token was simply the odd one out. The mirror settled the chart as Graves / Graves / Skill / Mundo / Mundo / Mundo / Graves and the two directions cannot disagree.
audit.corrected: diff FAV to match the 4/10 rating and the rest of the page. Chart: Level 2 to Graves, Level 3 to Skill, Level 6 to Dr. Mundo, 2+ items to Graves.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in six places and never given a number, and level 6 was written as a Graves spike.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17s at rank 1 — a real, repeatable trade window. Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank and instantly heals a percent of missing health, which is what actually decides the level-6 all-in, and it decides it his way.
audit.corrected: Heart Zapper is 17s at rank 1: trade in its downtime. Maximum Dosage is 120s and heals off missing health, so the lower you get him the more it returns — burst him from healthy or not at all.
sources: _kits/drmundo.json W cd 17/16.5/16/15.5/15, R cd 120 and text

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Buckshot' is used as a Graves ability in the TL;DR, the report and the early breakdown. Smoke Screen is called a blind three times. His passive is described as 'cheese-death regen'.
audit.why: Graves' shotgun is the passive New Destiny (four bullets that cannot pass through units); his Q is End of the Line. Smoke Screen reduces sight range and briefly slows. Riot's text for Goes Where He Pleases says he resists the first immobilizing effect, drops a cannister he can walk over to heal, and has significantly increased health regeneration — no death mechanic at all.
audit.corrected: New Destiny's four bullets cannot pass through units, so trade point-blank and off the wave. Smoke Screen slows and cuts his sight. His passive shrugs off the first immobilize entirely and drops a cannister he heals from — so your jungler's first CC on him is wasted, and that matters more than any regen line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned that a gank on Mundo starts a CC short.
audit.why: Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him. Any jungle setup on this lane has one CC eaten before the chain begins.
audit.corrected: His passive eats the first immobilize outright, so a gank needs two pieces of CC, not one — and he picks the cannister back up for health if you let him walk over it.

edits.before: Mundo's whole early game is a regen sponge, so your edge is the level-1 — walk up and unload a point-blank 4-shell spread plus an End of the Line cone before his passive cheese-death regen kicks in and before his cleaver out-trades you. Once he hits 3 and his Q percent-HP cleaver plus passive heals are online, stop facetanking: his cleaver scales off your fat health bar and his sustain eats your chip, so last-hit with the tip of your Q-cone and bank Quickdraw charges. Do not throw poke into a champ who heals it back for free — pick the all-in, not the trade war.
edits.after: Mundo's whole early game is a regen sponge, so your edge is level 1 — walk up and unload a point-blank 4-shell spread plus End of the Line before his health regen and Infected Bonesaw start out-trading you. Once he hits 3, stop facetanking: the cleaver scales off your health bar and his sustain eats chip damage, so last-hit with the tip of your Q and hold Quickdraw. Trade only in Heart Zapper's 17-second downtime, and remember his passive eats the first immobilize outright — a one-CC gank on him simply does not land.

edits.before: This is where Mundo is annoying — his first tank item plus passive regen lets him soak your shells and slow-cleaver you down at range, and his E (Blunt Force Trauma) adds bonus damage to his autos if you let him hit you. Note his Q costs a chunk of his current HP to cast, so bait it out, then Quickdraw in for the point-blank burst and drop a Smoke Screen to blind his empowered E auto so the trade lands your way. At 6 his R Maximum Dosage heals a huge slice of his max HP, so a solo all-in often just feeds his sustain unless you have a clean End of the Line plus Collateral Damage nuke ready or a jungler — duel him only when his cleaver is on cooldown.
edits.after: This is where Mundo is annoying — his first tank item plus passive regen lets him soak shells and cleaver you down from 975, and Blunt Force Trauma (E) passively scales his attack damage off his max health. Bait the cleaver, then Quickdraw in for the point-blank burst and drop Smoke Screen so the slow and sight cut buy your exit — it does not stop his damage. At 6 Maximum Dosage (120s) heals a percent of his MISSING health, so the harder you chunk him the more it returns; a solo all-in feeds it unless you open from full with End of the Line plus Collateral Damage, or bring your jungler.

notes: The diff token said HARD while diffRating, tone, breakdown.difficulty and report[14] all said favoured 4/10 — with a 60% win rate behind them. Fixed the token, not the four fields. 'Buckshot' used as a Graves ability in three fields (his shotgun is the passive New Destiny, his Q is End of the Line) — the mirrored Dr. Mundo audit found the same fabrication six times on its side. 'Smoke Screen blind' fixed in three places. The passive was described as 'cheese-death regen', which is not what Riot's text says — it resists the first immobilizing effect and drops a healing cannister, and that gank-relevant fact was missing from the page entirely. Level chart flipped as one group to the mirror's chart. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: the mid text claims Infected Bonesaw 'costs a chunk of his current HP to cast'. The kit file lists cost 0 and Riot's description says nothing about a health cost, so I could not confirm it and did not touch the sentence around it.
